theory.title: C2 Mastery: Language, Meaning and Expression
theory.explanation: This final C2 mission brings together advanced vocabulary, inference, register, grammatical control and clear expression across varied contexts. Focus on precision, cohesion and the ability to communicate complex ideas naturally and confidently.
theory.tip: At C2 level, choose the expression that best captures the intended meaning, register and degree of certainty; avoid unnecessary repetition.

patterns.label: Define the context
patterns.pattern: Identify the setting, audience and purpose before choosing vocabulary.
examples: The wording should reflect both the audience and the communicative purpose.

patterns.label: Add precision
patterns.pattern: Use specific terms and qualify claims where the evidence is limited.
examples: The available examples suggest a pattern, although further observation would be needed.

patterns.label: Develop a comparison
patterns.pattern: Compare alternatives by explaining the criteria that distinguish them.
examples: Unlike the earlier approach, the revised method places greater emphasis on consistency.

patterns.label: Synthesize ideas
patterns.pattern: Connect details into a coherent explanation rather than listing observations.
examples: Taken together, these features create a more nuanced account of the subject.

content.passage: Effective communication at an advanced level involves more than an extensive vocabulary. Speakers and writers must select language that suits the context, organise ideas coherently and signal the relationship between claims with precision. A sophisticated explanation may require qualification, comparison or a carefully chosen example. Concision is equally important: removing unnecessary repetition can strengthen an argument without oversimplifying it. Readers also need to distinguish what a text states explicitly from what it merely suggests. These skills develop through attentive reading, deliberate practice and reflection on how different audiences interpret the same message. The most successful communicators combine accuracy with flexibility, adapting their register while preserving clarity and purpose.
